name: Athens
overview: Athens, a prominent city of Greece, is depicted in Scripture as a center deeply immersed in idolatry, which stirred Paul’s spirit upon his arrival. There, Paul engaged both Jews and devout persons in the synagogue as well as philosophers in the marketplace, boldly proclaiming Jesus and the resurrection. His message was met with curiosity and skepticism, leading to his invitation to speak at the Areopagus, the highest court in Athens, where he was asked to explain this new doctrine. This account highlights the challenge and opportunity of presenting the gospel in a culture steeped in false beliefs.
